title: Higher FEMA expected-loss ratings coincide with higher observed insurance premiums and nonrenewal exposure
source_unit: Treasury FIO ZIP-code insurance market rows assigned to FEMA NRI county context through Census geographic relationships
geography: United States; 2022 Treasury ZIP rows, primary county by largest ZCTA land-area intersection, FEMA county baseline

observations.period: 2022 Treasury market rows matched to FEMA county context

matched_rows.unit: rows assigned to a FEMA NRI county

zctas_with_county_relationship.unit: ZCTAs in the Census relationship file

observations.method: Treasury ZIP values are matched to 2020 Census ZCTA codes; where a ZCTA intersects multiple counties, the county with the largest reported ZCTA land-area part is selected; the FEMA county EAL rating is attached.
observations.uncertainty: The county assignment discards secondary intersections; FEMA NRI is a modeled county baseline whose version and reference period are not the same as the 2022 insurance observations. Missing matches may be systematic.
observations.subgroup: Treasury ZIP rows grouped by FEMA Expected Annual Loss composite rating.
observations.counterinterpretation: The join does not establish that hazard causes a particular premium or nonrenewal; property values, rebuilding costs, insurer mix, regulation, policy composition, and reporting coverage may differ by county.

observations.period: 2022 Treasury market rows by FEMA Expected Annual Loss rating

denominator.unit: matched ZIP rows; unweighted row means

observations.method: Unweighted means of Treasury 2022 ZIP rows within FEMA NRI composite Expected Annual Loss rating groups, after area-based ZCTA-to-county assignment.
observations.uncertainty: Rating categories are modeled and the non-monotonic Very High premium result shows that rating bins do not substitute for continuous hazard, asset, or market controls. Means are not policy-weighted or household estimates.
observations.subgroup: FEMA NRI EAL ratings: Very Low, Relatively Low, Relatively Moderate, Relatively High, Very High.
observations.counterinterpretation: Relatively High has the highest mean premium in this screen while Very High has the highest mean nonrenewal; this is not a monotonic dose-response and should not be narrated as one.

related_sources.claim: FEMA documentation describes county expected annual loss construction and modeled-risk interpretation.
related_sources.access_boundary: A modeled risk index is not a realized insurance premium or household loss.

related_sources.claim: The local join output records matching, assignment, and rating-group summaries.
related_sources.access_boundary: The output is an unweighted descriptive screen, not a causal estimate.

boundary: This record adds hazard context to the insurance market/place bridge. It does not establish causal hazard pricing, insurer withdrawal, household affordability, coverage adequacy, repairs, lending, mobility, or political response.
